column1: Whisk the flour, salt, and yeast in a large bowl. Add the water and stir with a spatula until a sticky dough forms.
Optional: cover for 30 minutes, then with a wet hand do 8–10 rounds of stretching an edge up and folding it to the center until the dough feels smoother.
Coat the dough lightly with olive oil, cover tightly, and refrigerate for at least 12 hours and up to 3 days.
Grease a 9x13-inch pan or two 8- or 9-inch pie plates with butter (or line with parchment) and add 2 tbsp oil to the 9x13 pan or 1 tbsp to each pie plate.
Use two forks to deflate the dough into a rough ball, divide it if using two pans, and roll it in the oil to coat.
Leave uncovered at room temperature for 3–4 hours until puffy.
Preheat the oven to 425°F (218°C) with a rack in the middle.
Scatter rosemary over the dough if using, drizzle with the remaining oil, and press straight down with oiled fingers to make deep dimples, stretching to fill the pan. Sprinkle with flaky salt.
Bake 25–30 minutes until the bottom is golden and crisp.
Move to a cooling rack and let cool 10 minutes before slicing.
